opening_message:
Ticket 1: Christopher Myers (employee ID E012) requests write access to Source Code.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E012.
Note 1 (ticket 1):
  - role: Analyst
  - employment type: full_time
  - recommendation for Source Code: write
  - comment: Christopher Myers (E012) is a full-time Analyst requesting write access to Source Code. As a full-time employee, write is permitted (admin is only for the owning Engineer role). Recommend granting write.
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - role: Analyst
  - employment type: contractor
  - security training: basic
  - recommendation for Source Code: read
  - comment: Security DB shows E012 (Christopher Myers) is a contractor with basic security training, not full-time as previously noted. Contractors with basic training max out at read. Requested write to Source Code exceeds max, so recommend granting read.
reason: Security note for E012 indicates Christopher Myers is a contractor with basic security training (correcting the earlier full-time claim). Per policy, contractors may receive read, or write only with advanced security training. With basic training, max is read. Requested write exceeds max, so grant read.

content.text:
Let me analyze this ticket.

Christopher Myers (E012) requests write access to Source Code.

Two notes from team memory conflict:
- Note 1 (from HR agent): role Analyst, employment type full_time, recommendation write.
- Note 2 (from Security agent): role Analyst, employment type contractor, security training basic, recommendation read. Note claims Security DB shows contractor with basic training, not full-time.

The Security note appears to have newer/corrected information. But I need to decide based on available info. The security note says contractor, basic training. For contractors: read, or write if they have advanced security training. Never admin. Since basic training, max is read. Requested write > max read, so grant read.

But there's conflict between notes. The security agent's note explicitly corrects the HR note ("not full-time as previously noted"). I'll go with the security note: contractor with basic training => max read. Grant read.

Submit decision: read.
